newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index ends week with small gain.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index ends week with small gain.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with gains to Nafta pushing the SAX index up 2.22 points.
Brokers said they saw the market reviving after a month-long quiet period.

"It seems that the downward trend has stopped already," Patrik Granec of Slovenska Sporitelna said. "Decline was based probably on speculative grounds, rather than any general lack of confidence in the market," he said.
Trading on the bourse floor was dominated by oil and gas storage company Nafta, which closed down two crowns at 1,925. Nafta's average price was 0.57 percent higher with 20,004 shares traded.
Granec said there was also a revival in interest in steel maker VSZ and the country's biggest commercial bank VUB.
VSZ closed up five at 650 crowns, on volume of 36 shares, while VUB closed up 50 at 1,750 crowns, with 132 shares traded.
"I think VSZ has been boosted mainly by the latest company news, including those about the deal with Czech Trinecke Zelezarny," Granec added.
Overall, volume decreased to 408,901 shares, from 429,300 on Thursday, while turnover increased to 298.28 million crowns, from 239.19 million.
